about: Demo personas for the Personal Economic Trainer. Names are fictional; customer IDs and all numbers come from the synthetic dataset as of 2026-09-30 (BDA model run of 14 Nov 2026). Selected with scripts/select_personas.py; see demo/PERSONAS.md for the method and stories.

personas.name: Aino
personas.headline: Money runs out before payday
personas.story: Aino earns about €1,240 a month and spends a little more than that. The account goes negative most months, and September brought the biggest home & tech bill in two years. The coach shows where the money goes, why the month runs out, and one small change that breaks the cycle.

demo_questions.q: What is safe for me to spend this week?
demo_questions.expect: Nothing spare until payday on 15 Oct after rent, bills and essentials.

demo_questions.q: Why does my account keep going into the red?
demo_questions.expect: Over the last 12 months about €120/month more went out than came in (€1,320 in, €1,440 out); September was the biggest home & tech month in two years (€310 vs €65 usually).
Answer in Finnish: about half fixed bills, half everyday spending; restaurants are the biggest everyday line.

demo_questions.q: How much would I save if I cut entertainment by 20%?
demo_questions.expect: Computed by the what-if tool from the current entertainment level (about €100/month).

personas.name: Mikko
personas.headline: Doing fine, but money leaks after payday
personas.story: Mikko earns about €2,300, invests about €275 a month and has never been overdrawn. But nearly a fifth of all card spending happens in the three days after payday, restaurants and takeaways cost more than twice what peers pay per visit, and big one-off buys happen about three times a year. The coach makes the leaks visible without lecturing.
shows: peer comparison with the 'how often vs how much' split

facts.spender_type: Takeaway lover and Foodie (and a saver)

demo_questions.q: What kind of spender am I?
demo_questions.expect: Takeaway lover and foodie who also saves: eats out about as often as peers but spends about €70 vs €30 per restaurant visit and €65 vs €30 per takeaway.

demo_questions.q: How much could I save if I reduced dining out by 20%?
demo_questions.expect: Computed by the what-if tool; matching peers on restaurants alone saves about €70/month (€840/year).

demo_questions.q: Do I spend more right after payday?
demo_questions.expect: Yes: about 19% of card spending lands in the 3 days after payday, ~1.9x an even pace. (No backend tool for this yet.)

personas.name: Sanni
personas.headline: Saving steadily towards a first home
personas.story: Sanni earns about €2,300, automatically invests about €400 a month and spends little on extras. The balance grew from €7,700 to €13,500 in a year, and the model says another €350 a month could safely go to savings. The coach praises the habit and answers the big question: how close is a first home?
shows: home readiness using the bank's affordability rule (future tool)

home_affordability.rule: required monthly income = loan x 0.0184 (6% stress rate, 25-year annuity, 35% debt-to-income), derived exactly from the bank's mortgage data

demo_questions.q: How much have I saved this year?
demo_questions.expect: About €400/month invested (18% of income) and the balance grew by about €5,800 in 12 months.

demo_questions.q: Could I afford my own home?
demo_questions.expect: Illustration only: income supports a loan of about €125k under the bank's stress test, i.e. a ~€139k home with a 10% (~€13.9k) deposit. Suggest the bank's advisor. (Needs a future tool.)
Already lean: restaurants about €25/month vs €120 for peers. The model says about €350/month more could safely go to savings (€4,200/year).

personas.name: Pekka
personas.headline: A surprise bill a week before payday
personas.story: Pekka earns well (about €4,350) and invests about €435 a month, yet on 8 Aug 2026 a €1,294 home & tech payment a week before payday left €281 in the account, and groceries pushed it below zero until salary arrived on the 15th. Surprise costs like this hit about four times a year, and right now money is tight again until payday. The coach explains the 'mandatory but irregular' basket and how a surprise fund prevents the next one.
shows: explaining a past event from transactions

demo_questions.q: Why did my account go negative in August?
demo_questions.expect: A €1,294 home & tech payment on 8 Aug, a week before payday; the balance fell to €281 and groceries took it below zero on 10 Aug until salary on 15 Aug.

demo_questions.q: What is safe for me to spend this week?
demo_questions.expect: Nothing spare until payday on 15 Oct after rent, bills and essentials.

demo_questions.q: How do I prepare for surprise costs?
demo_questions.expect: They hit ~4 times a year at ~€1,100; a €7,200 surprise fund covers a bad year and the balance is ~€4,350 short: about €340/month on payday, ready in ~13 months.
